iut_type: Internal business economics note -- relative profitability and effort of handling Japan TELEC/Giteki radio-law certification cases versus Bluetooth Logo certification
customer_question: (Internal note, not a customer question.) Should the sales team take on requests involving Japan's domestic radio-law (Giteki) certification (TELEC) alongside Bluetooth Logo certification requests?
question_variants: Is handling a TELEC/Giteki certification case as profitable, relative to effort, as handling a Bluetooth Logo certification case?
actual_issue: A sales team member was preparing to handle a customer's combined Bluetooth and Japan radio-law (Giteki/TELEC) certification questions, and an internal note flagged the comparative economics of taking on the Giteki/TELEC side of the work.
plain_english_explanation: As an internal point of reference: handling a Japan TELEC (radio-law construction design certification) case billed at ¥366,000 yields Allion a profit of only about ¥15,000 -- a thin margin relative to the billed amount. Moreover, the effort required for customers who use Giteki/radio-law terminology and concepts tends to be disproportionately larger compared to a Bluetooth Logo certification case of similar billing size, since the two regulatory regimes have different rules, terminology, and customer expectations that require separate explanation and handling.
consultant_answer: For reference, the profit margin on a ¥366,000 TELEC case is only about ¥15,000, and the effort required for customers operating at a Giteki/radio-law level of detail is disproportionately larger than for Bluetooth Logo certification -- worth keeping in mind when scoping combined engagements.
decision_logic: When evaluating whether to take on a customer's combined Bluetooth and Japan radio-law (TELEC/Giteki) certification request, account for the comparatively thin profit margin and disproportionately higher effort that radio-law-side work tends to require relative to Bluetooth Logo certification work of similar billing size.
final_recommendation: When scoping a request that bundles Bluetooth Logo certification with Japan radio-law (TELEC/Giteki) certification, factor in the comparatively low margin and higher effort intensity of the radio-law side before committing significant team time to it.
risk_if_done_wrong: Underestimating the effort-to-profit ratio of TELEC/Giteki work bundled with a Bluetooth engagement could result in disproportionate time investment relative to the revenue generated.
